record.title: The bioriented-cycle subdivision conjecture
record.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph, let $\vec{\chi}(D)$ denote its dichromatic number, and let $\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{C}_\ell$ denote the bioriented cycle of length $\ell$. **Bioriented-cycle subdivision conjecture.** If $D$ has $\vec{\chi}(D)\ge3$, then there exists an integer $\ell\ge3$ such that $D$ contains a subdivision of $\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{C}_\ell$. Equivalently, the maximum dichromatic number of a digraph containing no subdivision of any bioriented cycle should be $2$. This remains an open question about forcing bioriented-cycle subdivisions in digraphs.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Dichromatic number and forced subdivisions”, arXiv:2008.09888 (2020).

record.title: Dual minimum-distance conjecture for the code of the design ${\mathbb{D}}$
record.statement:
Let ${\mathbb{D}}$ be the design defined earlier in the paper, and let ${\mathsf{C}}_p({\mathbb{D}})^\perp$ denote the dual of its code over the field of characteristic $p$. **Dual minimum-distance conjecture.** The minimum distance of ${\mathsf{C}}_p({\mathbb{D}})^\perp$ equals

$$
q+1.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by experimental data. The surrounding theorem establishes only the lower bound $d^\perp\geq 3$ in general and identifies $d^\perp=p+1$ when $q=p$, so the asserted value remains unresolved in the supplied text for general $q$.
record.source_name: Cunsheng Ding and Chunming Tang, “The linear codes of t-designs held in the Reed-Muller and Simplex codes”, arXiv:2008.09935 (2020).

record.title: Gorsky–Neguț–Rasmussen conjecture on coherent computation of Khovanov–Rozansky homology
record.statement:
Let $F_\beta$ be the Rouquier complex associated to a braid $\beta$, let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the tautological bundle on the dg flag Hilbert scheme, and let $\iota_*$ and $\iota^*$ be the adjoint functors in the preceding conjecture. Write $\int$ for pushforward to a point in the coherent equivariant category.

**Gorsky–Neguț–Rasmussen conjecture.** There is an isomorphism of bigraded vector spaces

$$
\operatorname{HHH}^{k}(F_\beta)\simeq\operatorname{HH}^{0}\bigl(\iota^*(\wedge^k\mathcal{T}_n^{\vee})\otimes F_\beta\bigr)\simeq\int \iota_*(F_\beta)\otimes\wedge^k\mathcal{T}_n^{\vee}.
$$

The proposed formula would compute Khovanov–Rozansky homology on the coherent side of the flag-Hilbert-scheme model. The paper describes it as a prediction from the cited conjecture, not as a theorem.

record.title: Concavity conjecture for the maximum m-field of the symmetric group
record.statement:
Let $n$ be fixed. For a partition of the symmetric group $\mathbb{S}_n$ into $m$ parts, let $F(n,m)$ denote the maximum attainable sum of intensities, and define

$$
f(m)=F(n,m).
$$

**Concavity conjecture.** For any fixed $n$, the function $f(m)=F(n,m)$ is concave.

The conjecture is proposed as a way to understand the growth of $F(n,m)$ beyond the polynomial range, where the paper's upper bounds are far from the available lower bound. No proof is given.
record.source_name: Artur Czumaj, George Kontogeorgiou and Mike Paterson, “Haystack Hunting Hints and Locker Room Communication”, arXiv:2008.11448 (2021).
record.references:

record.title: Latin-strategy characterization conjecture for the symmetric group
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A **Latin strategy** is obtained by choosing an $n\times n$ Latin square $S$; Alice's message identifies a row of $S$ that agrees with the input permutation at the maximum possible number of positions. An optimal strategy is one attaining the maximum success probability.

**Latin-strategy characterization conjecture.** Optimal strategies are exactly Latin strategies.

This conjecture proposes a complete characterization of optimal strategies, extending the explicitly described shift strategies. The paper states it as an open question and does not prove the characterization.

record.title: Finite-time wave breaking criterion for the generalized 0-Holm-Staley equation
record.statement:
Let $k=1$, let $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb{R})$ with $s>3/2$, and let $u$ be the corresponding solution of equation (8.0.1), with lifespan $T$. **Finite-time wave breaking conjecture.** The solution $u$ breaks at finite time if and only if

$$
\lim_{t\nearrow T}|u_x(t,x)|=+\infty.
$$

The authors present this as a provocation because they prove a necessary condition for wave breaking but are unable to find sufficient conditions. The conjecture therefore remains open in the source.

record.title: Quasi-star or quasi-clique conjecture for path supersaturation
record.statement: Let $k$ and $\ell$ be positive integers with $k>\ell$. For an $n$-vertex graph containing at least $m$ copies of the path $P_k$, let $\operatorname{satex}(n,P_k:m,P_{\ell})$ denote the minimum number of copies of $P_{\ell}$. **Path quasi-star or quasi-clique conjecture.** The minimum is attained asymptotically by either a quasi-star or a quasi-clique. The source gives no resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: Subdivision-preservation conjecture for maderian digraphs
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a digraph. A **subdivision** of $F$ is obtained by replacing each arc with a directed path, with the replacement paths internally vertex-disjoint. Say that $F$ is $\delta^+$-maderian if sufficiently large minimum out-degree forces a subdivision of $F$.

**Subdivision-preservation conjecture.** If a digraph $F$ is $\delta^+$-maderian, all subdivisions of $F$ are $\delta^+$-maderian as well.

The statement is presented as a plausible preservation principle and remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Raphael Steiner and Tibor Szabó, “Oriented cycles in digraphs of large outdegree”, arXiv:2008.13224 (2020).

record.title: The connectivity bound for monochromatic disconnection numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ that is **$k$-connected**, meaning that deleting fewer than $k$ vertices does not disconnect $G$ or reduce it to a single vertex. Let $md(G)$ denote the maximum number of colors allowed in an edge-coloring of $G$ such that every pair of distinct vertices is separated by a monochromatic edge-cut. **Connectivity bound conjecture.**

$$
md(G)\leq \left\lfloor\frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor.
$$

The paper notes that this bound is known when $k=2$ and when $k\geq \left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor$, while the general case is left as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Ping Li and Xueliang Li, “Upper bounds for the MD-numbers and characterization of extremal graphs”, arXiv:2009.00222 (2020).

record.title: Erdős's girth conjecture
record.statement: Let $l,n$ be positive integers. A graph with girth $2l+1$ and $n$ vertices is said to have many edges if its number of edges is bounded below by a positive constant times $n^{1+\frac{1}{l}}$. **Erdős's conjecture.** For any positive integers $l,n$, there exists a graph with girth $2l+1$, $n$ vertices and $\Omega(n^{1+\frac{1}{l}})$ edges. This conjecture concerns the extremal number of edges in graphs of prescribed odd girth and is related to the sharpness of upper bounds for graph radius in terms of minimum degree and girth.
record.source_name: Vojtěch Dvořák, Peter van Hintum, Amy Shaw and Marius Tiba, “Radius, Girth and Minimum Degree”, arXiv:2009.00741 (2020).
record.references:

record.title: Maximum Möbius value conjecture for rank-3 intervals in the matching pattern poset
record.statement:
Let $U$ and $D$ denote up and down steps, respectively, and let $[P,Q]$ be an interval in the matching pattern poset of Dyck paths. An interval has rank $3$ when its endpoints differ in semilength by $3$, and $\mu$ denotes the Möbius function of this poset.

**Rank-3 maximum conjecture.** The maximum absolute value of the Möbius function on intervals of rank $3$ is

$$
(2n+1)\cdot n^2,
$$

attained by the interval

$$
[U(UD)^{n-1}D,U(UD)^{n+2}D].
$$

This conjecture is supported by computations; it predicts the extremal Möbius value among rank-3 intervals but does not assert uniqueness of the attaining interval.
record.source_name: Matteo Cervetti and Luca Ferrari, “Pattern avoidance in the matching pattern poset”, arXiv:2009.01024 (2020).

record.title: Directed discrete filling area conjecture for fine surfaces
record.statement:
Let $C=C_{a,b}$ be a fine cycle whose two oriented lengths are $a$ and $b$, and let $M$ be a regular fine surface with boundary $C$. Its area is the number of fine triangles it contains. **Directed discrete FAC, or fine FAC.** If $M$ fills $C$ isometrically, then

$$
\operatorname{Area}(M)\geq 2ab-a-b.
$$

This is the discrete directed counterpart of the directed Finsler filling area conjecture; the source notes that fine fillings exist and that the minimum depends only on $a$ and $b$.
record.source_name: Marcos Cossarini, “Discrete surfaces with length and area and minimal fillings of the circle”, arXiv:2009.02415 (2020).

record.title: Injective coloring conjecture for regular uniform hypergraphs
record.statement: Let $r\geq 2$. An **injective $q$-coloring** of an $r$-uniform hypergraph is a coloring of its vertices with $q$ colors such that any two edges sharing $r-1$ vertices have distinct color sets. **Injective coloring conjecture.** There exist constants $c,c'>0$ such that, whenever $H$ is a $\Delta$-regular $r$-graph with maximum $(r-1)$-degree at most $D$, $H$ has a spanning subgraph $G$ of minimum degree at least $c\Delta$ with an injective $c'D$-coloring. The source notes that an injectively colored subgraph with linearly many edges is already available; the open difficulty is preserving minimum degree, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Sam Spiro and Jacques Verstraëte, “Relative Turán Problems for Uniform Hypergraphs”, arXiv:2009.02416 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02416

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2020). “The main open question for relative Tur\'{a}n numbers of $r$-graphs is to give bounds on $\ex(H,F)$ when $F$ is $r$-partite.”

record.title: Modified clique-free diameter conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$, let $\delta\geq \left\lceil\frac{3k}{2}\right\rceil-1$, and let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$ and minimum degree at least $\delta$. The graph is assumed to be $K_{k+1}$-free; the source also gives the weaker alternative hypothesis that $G$ is $k$-colorable.

**Modified diameter conjecture.** Under either the $K_{k+1}$-free hypothesis, or the weaker $k$-colorable hypothesis, one should have

$$
\operatorname{diam}(G)\leq\left(3-\frac{2}{k}\right)\frac{n}{\delta}+O(1).
$$

This modification is proposed after the even-clique case of the earlier conjecture is counterexampled. The paper presents it as a replacement conjecture; the $k$-colorable version is explicitly identified as weaker, and no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Éva Czabarka, Inne Singgih and László A. Székely, “On the maximum diameter of k-colorable graphs”, arXiv:2009.02611 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02611

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2020). “The counterexample leads to a modification of Conjecture , which no longer requires cases:”

record.title: Karthick's star-chi-boundedness conjecture for claw-free graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, the **star chromatic number** $\chi_s(G)$ is the minimum number of colors in a proper coloring such that any two color classes induce a star forest. A graph is **$K_{1,t}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,t}$. **Karthick's conjecture.** The class of all $K_{1,t}$-free graphs, where $t\geq 3$, is $\chi_s$-bounded.

This conjecture concerns star colorings under a natural forbidden-induced-subgraph condition. The supplied text gives no resolution status, while noting that Karthick introduced the notion of $\chi_s$-boundedness and proposed this conjecture.
record.source_name: Y. Jiang, J. Nesetril and P. Ossona de Mendez, “From χ- to χ_p-bounded classes”, arXiv:2009.02953 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02953

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2020). “This conjecture was disproved by Pawlik, Kozik, Krawczyk, Laso\'n, Micek, Trotter and Walczak .”

record.title: Karthick's star-chi-boundedness conjecture for $(T,C_4)$-free graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $F$, an **$F$-free** graph has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $F$; a graph is **$(T,C_4)$-free** if it is both $T$-free and $C_4$-free. Here $\chi_s$ denotes the star chromatic number, the minimum number of colors in a proper coloring in which any two color classes induce a star forest. **Karthick's conjecture.** For any tree $T$, the class of all $(T,C_4)$-free graphs is $\chi_s$-bounded.

This is one of the star-boundedness questions attributed to Karthick and restricts the forbidden induced subgraphs to a tree together with the four-cycle. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Y. Jiang, J. Nesetril and P. Ossona de Mendez, “From χ- to χ_p-bounded classes”, arXiv:2009.02953 (2021).

record.title: Grinshpun's conjecture on Ramsey-simple triangle-free graphs
record.statement: Let $H$ be a connected triangle-free graph. A graph $H$ is **$2$-Ramsey-simple** when $s_2(H)=2(\delta(H)-1)+1$, where $s_2(H)$ is the minimum degree that can occur in a minimal $2$-Ramsey graph for $H$. **Grinshpun's conjecture.** Every connected triangle-free graph is $2$-Ramsey-simple. This strengthens the known result that all $3$-connected bipartite graphs are $2$-Ramsey-simple and would imply the conjecture of Szabó et al. that every bipartite graph with no isolated vertices is $2$-Ramsey-simple; its status is not resolved in the source.

record.title: The independence conjecture for sum-free inverse-closed subsets of finite fields
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a finite field. Write $\sigma(\mathbb{F})$ for the density of the largest sum-free subset of $\mathbb{F}$, and $\mu(\mathbb{F})$ for the density of the largest subset of $\mathbb{F}$ that is both sum-free and closed under multiplicative inverses.

**Independence conjecture.**

$$
\mu(\mathbb{F})=\sigma(\mathbb{F})^{2}+o(1)
$$

as $|\mathbb{F}|\mathbin{\to}\infty$.

The conjecture expresses the expectation that the properties of being sum-free and having a sum-free inverse set behave independently. It would make the previously established lower bounds in characteristics $2$ and greater than $2$ asymptotically sharp.

record.title: Convexity conjecture for the hypergraph-based polynomial $f_d$
record.statement:
Let $n,L,d\geq 2$ be integers, let $f_d$ be the polynomial

$$
f_d(x)=\sum_{(e_1,\ldots,e_d)\in E^d}\prod_{i=1}^{d}\frac{x_{e_i}}{\lvert e_1\cup\cdots\cup e_i\rvert},
$$

and let $\Delta_m$ be the simplex on which it is defined. **Convexity conjecture.** The polynomial $f_d$ is convex over the simplex $\Delta_m$. This conjecture would give a positive answer to the question of whether $f_d$ attains its minimum on $\Delta_m$ at the barycenter, since a convex function with the relevant symmetry has that property. The source provides no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: The complexity hypothesis for typical three-dimensional billiards
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the upper bound on the number of smooth pieces into which the $n$th iterate of a smooth convex expanding submanifold is chopped by the billiard map. **Complexity hypothesis.** For typical three-dimensional billiards with smooth scatterers and finite horizon, there exists a number $\lambda>1$, strictly less than the smallest expansion rate on the unstable cones of the billiard, such that

$$
K_n=o(\lambda^n).
$$
Here typicality may be understood, for example, with respect to the $C^r$ topology on the scatterers for $r\geq 3$. The hypothesis is intended to control the effect of singularities relative to hyperbolicity and is presented as an open assumption needed for extending correlation-decay results to higher-dimensional billiards.
record.source_name: Péter Bálint, Thomas Gilbert, Domokos Szász and Imre Péter Tóth, “What mathematical billiards teach us about statistical physics?”, arXiv:2009.06284 (2020).

record.title: The conjectured bipartite minimum-degree threshold $d_{r,r}$
record.statement:
Let $d_{r,r}$ denote the parameter defined in the paper’s bipartite minimum-degree theorem, and let $r$ be a positive integer. **Bipartite minimum-degree threshold conjecture.** We have

$$
d_{r,r}=\left\lceil\frac{3r+1}{4}\right\rceil.
$$
 This conjecture predicts the exact bipartite minimum-degree threshold and is presented as a desired improvement of the paper’s estimates; its resolution is not supplied in the source.

record.title: Axis-symmetry conjecture for largest small even polygons
record.statement: For even $n\geq 6$, let $\mathtt{U}_n$ denote a largest small $n$-gon, and let its **diameter graph** be the graph whose vertices are the polygon's vertices and whose edges join pairs at distance one. A **pending edge** is the additional edge attached to the cycle of length $n-1$ in the diameter graph. **Axis-symmetry conjecture.** The polygon $\mathtt{U}_n$ has an axis of symmetry corresponding to the pending edge in its diameter graph. The source presents this as a conjectural symmetry property of the largest small even polygons, and gives no resolution status.

record.title: The strictly upper triangular holonomy conjecture for a model manifold with density
record.statement:
Let $M^n$ carry the metric

$$
g = e^{x_1}dx_1^2 + e^{2x_1+x_2}dx_2^2 + \cdots + e^{2x_1+\cdots+2x_{n-1}+x_n}dx_n^2
$$

and density potential $\phi=x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n$. Compute the holonomy Lie algebra at the origin $(0,0,\ldots,0)$. **Strictly upper triangular holonomy conjecture.** The holonomy Lie algebra is precisely the Lie algebra of strictly upper triangular matrices. This conjecture generalizes the explicitly verified two- and three-dimensional examples, where the holonomy is respectively the corresponding strictly upper triangular group; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

record.title: Borodin–Broersma–Glebov–van den Heuvel conjecture on cyclic coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph, let $\Delta^*(G)$ be its maximum face degree, and let $k^*=k^*(G)$ denote the maximum number of vertices that two faces of $G$ can have in common. A cyclic coloring assigns distinct colors to any two different vertices incident with the same face.

**Borodin–Broersma–Glebov–van den Heuvel conjecture.** Every plane graph $G$ with $\Delta^*(G)$ and $k^*$ sufficiently large has a cyclic coloring with

$$
\Delta^*(G)+k^*
$$

colors.

This conjecture refines the general cyclic-coloring problem by incorporating the overlap parameter $k^*$. The source presents it as an open question posed by Borodin, Broersma, Glebov, and van den Heuvel; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Stanislav Jendrol and Roman Sotak, “On the cyclic coloring conjecture”, arXiv:2009.10436 (2020).

record.title: Cyclic coloring conjecture for subdivisions of simple 3-connected plane graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subdivision of a simple $3$-connected plane graph. Define $t(G)$ to be the maximum number of subdivision vertices on an edge of the underlying graph, and let $\Delta^*(G)$ be the maximum face degree. Write $\chi_c(G)$ for the minimum number of colors in a cyclic coloring, meaning a vertex coloring in which vertices incident with the same face receive distinct colors.

**Subdivision cyclic coloring conjecture.** Every such graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi_c(G) \leq \Delta^*(G)+t(G)+2.
$$

The source introduces this as a new conjecture combining the Plummer–Toft conjecture with the corresponding subdivision case of the earlier conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Kalai–Meshulam chromatic conjecture on induced cycles
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let the chromatic number of $G$ be its minimum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring. An **induced cycle** is a cycle whose vertices induce exactly the edges of the cycle.

**Kalai–Meshulam chromatic conjecture.** A graph with high enough chromatic number has an induced cycle of length divisible by three.

This conjecture was proved by Bonamy, Charbit, and Thomassé, and later generalized by Scott and Seymour.

record.title: Jeon–Jin conjecture on knots with superbridge index three
record.statement: A knot's **superbridge index** is the minimum, over all embeddings of the knot in Euclidean three-space, of the maximum number of local maxima of the height function over all directions. **Jeon–Jin conjecture.** The only knots with superbridge index equal to $3$ are $3_1$ and $4_1$. This would classify all knots of superbridge index three; the paper states that the superbridge index remains unknown for the knots under consideration except for $3_1$ and $4_1$, so the conjecture is not resolved there.

record.title: The injective chromatic index conjecture for subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, meaning that its maximum degree is at most $3$. The **subcubic injective edge-coloring conjecture.**

$$
\chi'_{\rm inj}(G)\leq 6.
$$

The injective chromatic index is the minimum number of colors in an injective edge coloring, and the conjecture would improve the general bounds known for graphs of maximum degree three. It is attributed in the source to Ferdjallah, Kerdjoudj, and Raspaud.

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the SY class of a curve
record.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve in the setting above, and let the **SY torsor** of $X$ parametrize the choices used to construct its SY bundles. Each element of this torsor determines an **SY class** in $\operatorname{Br}(X^{(2)})[2]$, namely the class of the corresponding SY bundle, which is trivial if and only if that bundle admits a section. **Uniqueness conjecture for the SY class.** There is only one SY class associated to $X$; equivalently, the construction is independent of the choice of an element of the SY torsor. The claim is presented as plausible but unverified; it is known when $k$ is finite or algebraically closed, with additional supporting evidence for supersingular elliptic curves.

record.title: Restricted smallest-root conjecture for incomplete positive linear recurrence sequences
record.statement:
Let $L\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, let

$$
N_L=\left\lceil\frac{L(L+1)}{4}\right\rceil,
$$

and let $\lambda_L$ be the principal root of

$$
x^L-x^{L-1}-N_L-1.
$$

**Restricted smallest-root conjecture.** If the sequence generated by $[c_1,\ldots,c_L]$ is incomplete and satisfies

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{L}c_i\leq \left\lceil\frac{L(L+1)}{4}\right\rceil+2,
$$

then its principal root is at least $\lambda_L$. This is a restricted version of the proposed lower bound for incomplete sequences; the source provides motivation and partial analysis but no proof of the stated claim.
record.source_name: Elżbieta Bołdyriew, John Haviland, Phúc Lâm, John Lentfer, Steven J. Miller and Fernando Trejos Suárez, “Completeness of Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences”, arXiv:2010.01655 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.01655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

record.title: Planar 3-uniform hypergraph analogue of the Boots–Royle–Cao–Vince conjecture
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a planar $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices, and let its shadow be the graph obtained by replacing each hyperedge by the edges joining its pairs of vertices. Let $K_2+P_{n-2}$ denote the join of $K_2$ and the path $P_{n-2}$. **Planar hypergraph spectral-radius conjecture.** For sufficiently large $n$, the $n$-vertex planar $3$-uniform hypergraph of maximum spectral radius is the unique maximal hypergraph whose shadow is $K_2+P_{n-2}$. This is proposed as an analogue of the planar graph extremal conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: M. N. Ellingham, Linyuan Lu and Zhiyu Wang, “Maximum spectral radius of outerplanar 3-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:2010.04624 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04624

record.title: Additivity conjecture for the bad-domain invariant of non-alternating knots
record.statement:
Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be non-alternating knots. For a knot $K$, let $\beta(K)$ denote the minimum number of bad domains over diagrams representing $K$, and let $K_1\# K_2$ denote their connected sum. **Connected-sum conjecture.**

$$
\beta(K_1\# K_2)=\beta(K_1)+\beta(K_2)-2.
$$

The preceding construction gives the corresponding upper bound by taking connected sums of diagrams at bad edges; the conjecture asserts that this bound is always sharp for non-alternating knots. It is motivated by the additivity of knot Floer homology thickness, while the behavior of $\beta$ under connected sum is otherwise unclear.
record.source_name: Andras I. Stipsicz and Zoltan Szabo, “A note on thickness of knots”, arXiv:2010.04967 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2004–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0403326](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0403326).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04967

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

record.title: Brouwer's toughness conjecture for regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $d$-regular graph, let $t(G)$ denote its toughness, and let $\lambda$ be the second largest absolute eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of $G$. **Brouwer's toughness conjecture.** For any connected $d$-regular graph $G$, 

$$
t(G)\ge \frac{d}{\lambda}-1.
$$

Brouwer's conjecture strengthens his eigenvalue bound $t(G)>\frac{d}{\lambda}-2$; partial results are known, but the source states that no substantial progress had been made for more than two decades before the paper's proof.
record.source_name: Xiaofeng Gu, “A proof of Brouwer's toughness conjecture”, arXiv:2010.05065 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.05065

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Smallest Fibonacci-run graph containing a hypercube
record.statement:
Let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph, and let $\mathcal{R}_m$ denote the Fibonacci-run graph of parameter $m$. **Hypercube embedding conjecture.** The smallest integer $m$ for which $Q_n$ can be embedded into $\mathcal{R}_m$ is

$$
m=\left\lceil\frac{5n-4}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This is motivated by calculations from the cube-polynomial generating function and the claimed embeddings of $Q_{2m+1}$ in $\mathcal{R}_{5m+1}$ and $Q_{2m+2}$ in $\mathcal{R}_{5m+3}$, but the optimality assertion remains unproved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ömer Eğecioğlu and Vesna Iršič, “Fibonacci-run graphs II: Degree sequences”, arXiv:2010.05521 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.05521

record.title: Uniqueness and equal distribution conjecture for least-gradient sections
record.statement: Let $L$ be the flat affine bundle and let $v:M\to L$ be the BV section from Theorem~, obtained as a limit of the $q$-harmonic maps. **Least-gradient section conjecture.** The BV section $v:M\to L$ is unique, and the limit $v$ is equally distributed. Equivalently, the associated cohomology class and least-gradient section should be uniquely determined, with the resulting transverse measure giving equal weight to the components. The paper explains that uniqueness would determine the transverse measure associated with a possibly disconnected maximum stretch lamination, but the authors cannot prove it.
record.source_name: Georgios Daskalopoulos and Karen Uhlenbeck, “Transverse Measures and Best Lipschitz and Least Gradient Maps”, arXiv:2010.06551 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06551

record.title: The local obstruction conjecture for Bernoulli matrix singularity
record.statement:
Let $B_n(p)$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with independent and identically distributed Bernoulli entries of mean $p$, and let $q_n(p)=\mathbb{P}[B_n(p)\text{ is singular}]$. **Local obstruction conjecture.** For fixed $p\in(0,1)$,

$$
q_n(p)=(1+o_n(1))\mathbb{P}[B_n(p)\emph{ has two equal rows, two equal columns, a zero row, or a zero column}].
$$

The conjecture asserts that singularity is asymptotically caused by these elementary local obstructions. The paper presents it as a natural extension of a folklore conjecture and notes that the available result of Tikhomirov does not determine the required sharp error term.
record.source_name: Vishesh Jain, Ashwin Sah and Mehtaab Sawhney, “Sharp invertibility of random Bernoulli matrices”, arXiv:2010.06553 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06553

record.title: Linial's universal surface extremal-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{hom}(n,\mathcal{S})$ denote the maximum number of edges in a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no hypergraph homeomorphic to $\mathcal{S}$. **Linial's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(\mathcal{H})>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{hom}(n,\mathcal{S})<cn^{5/2}.
$$

The conjecture is the general form of the proposed $O(n^{5/2})$ bound for avoiding a fixed topological hypergraph; the paper has established the bound for triangulations of orientable surfaces, while the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Andrey Kupavskii, Alexandr Polyanskii, István Tomon and Dmitriy Zakharov, “The extremal number of surfaces”, arXiv:2010.07191 (2020).

record.title: Optimal Gonality Conjecture for optimal curves
record.statement:
Let $C$ be an optimal curve over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ of genus $g$, meaning that it has $N_q(g)$ rational points. The **geometric gonality** of a curve is the minimum degree of a morphism from its base change to $\mathbb{P}^1$ over the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q$.

**Optimal Gonality Conjecture.** Every optimal curve $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of genus $g$ has gonality at most $\operatorname{geomgon}$.

The conjecture predicts that optimal curves have especially low gonality. It holds for $q=2,3,4$ and $g\leq 5$, and also for $q=2$ and $g=6$; the source gives further examples in genera $7$, $8$, and $9$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
record.source_name: Xander Faber and Jon Grantham, “Ternary and Quaternary Curves of Small Fixed Genus and Gonality with Many Rational Points”, arXiv:2010.07992 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07992

record.title: The semibrick-pair completion conjecture for tau-tilting finite algebras
record.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a $\tau$-tilting finite algebra, and let $\mathcal{D} \sqcup \mathcal{U}[1]$ be a **semibrick pair**, meaning a collection of bricks in the indicated degrees satisfying the relevant hom-orthogonality conditions. Let the smallest wide subcategory containing $\mathcal{D}\sqcup \mathcal{U}[1]$ be the wide subcategory generated by this pair. **Semibrick-pair completion conjecture.** The pair $\mathcal{D} \sqcup \mathcal{U}[1]$ is completable if and only if the smallest wide subcategory containing it has $|\mathcal{D}| + |\mathcal{U}|$ simple objects. This concerns when semibrick pairs extend to 2-term simple minded collections in the $\tau$-tilting finite setting; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Emily Barnard and Eric J. Hanson, “Pairwise Compatibility for 2-Simple Minded Collections II: Preprojective Algebras and Semibrick Pairs of Full Rank”, arXiv:2010.08645 (2023).

record.title: Ellipse-locus conjecture for triangle centers on focus-mounted triangles
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be an ellipse with foci $f_1$ and $f_2$, and let $P(t)$ sweep $\mathcal{E}$. For the triangle $\mathcal{T}_f(t)=f_1f_2P(t)$, denote by $X_k$ the $k$th triangle center, and let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be the first and second triangle centers. A point $X_k$ is a **fixed affine combination** of $X_1$ and $X_2$ if there are constants independent of $t$ such that $X_k=\lambda X_1+(1-\lambda)X_2$. **Ellipse-locus conjecture.** The locus of $X_k$ over $\mathcal{T}_f(t)=f_1f_2P(t)$ is an ellipse if and only if $X_k$ is a fixed affine combination of $X_1$ and $X_2$. Numerical analysis found no counterexample among the more than 38,000 listed centers that are not on the $X_1X_2$ line, while the proposition preceding the conjecture identifies several centers whose loci are ellipses. The claim remains unproved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Mark Helman, Ronaldo Garcia and Dan Reznik, “Intriguing Invariants of Centers of Ellipse-Inscribed Triangles”, arXiv:2010.09408 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.09408

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).
